text: Working with APIs is a fundamental skill for modern developers. When you interact with an API, you typically send HTTP requests to a server, such as GET to retrieve data or POST to send new information. The server usually responds with data in JSON format, which is easy for both humans and machines to read. To access protected resources, you often need authentication, like an API key or a token. Remember that most APIs have rate limits, meaning you can only make a certain number of requests in a given time. Finally, always include error handling in your code, because network issues or bad inputs can cause requests to fail. This way, your application can respond gracefully instead of crashing.
